epigraph: Stand still. The ground holds its breath.
vignette: The stone did not break. It simply stopped being dirt. A man pressed his palm to the mud. He thought of weight. He thought of the mountain that does not move. The earth listened. It rose. It became a wall of gray rock. It was ten feet high. It was five feet thick. It did not glow. It did not sing. It just was. The Verdant vine tried to climb it. The vine snapped. The Umbral fire tried to melt it. The fire cooled. The Colossus stood. It was not alive. It was not dead. It was a fact. The other side pushed against it. Their wolf ran into the stone. The wolf fell back. Their glass tree grew toward the shadow. The tree stopped. The ground believed in the stone. The stone believed in itself. Nothing else mattered. The line held. The air was still. The dust settled on the flat top. The man walked away. The wall remained. It was heavy. It was true. That was enough.
codex_note: The Colossus requires no complex ritual, only the absolute refusal to yield space.
